title: Does a Reaction Ever Stop? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
In an ammonia factory, nitrogen and hydrogen never turn fully into ammonia. In your blood, haemoglobin picks up oxygen in the lungs and lets it go in the muscles. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Aarav asks: when a reaction looks finished halfway, has it stopped, or is it secretly running?

You will see dynamic equilibrium as walking down an up escalator, then heat hydrogen and iodine on the molecule bench and watch H2 + I2 make HI while HI breaks back, with live counts and a rate graph where the forward and backward rates meet. We define reversible reactions, rate and concentration, read the rate and concentration graphs step by step, show that equilibrium is reached from either direction, and walk through the deuterium test that found NH2D, NHD2 and HD. Then a worked example, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 59 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
